findings.title: Two independent bill-required flags on one claim type
findings.problem: requires_bill and bill_required express the same bill-required decision but are stored independently without an equality constraint or reconciliation. The current entitlement reader uses bill_required; the earlier taxonomy seeded requires_bill. Submission always requires a bill regardless of either value. is_taxable and taxable_if_unsubstantiated are different concepts and must not be merged just because both are booleans.
findings.decision: Canonicalize the bill policy after comparing existing values and the two workflows; expose one authoritative value. Keep current-claim taxability separate from year-end taxability on unsubstantiated entitlement. Use expand/contract compatibility before retiring a proven duplicate. No column was dropped.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass

findings.title: Raw pre-join token persists alongside its hash
findings.problem: Creation stores both rawToken and tokenHash; lookup uses the hash. Raw credential retention defeats the benefit of hashing. Validation and completion update are separate operations. link_sent and sent_at are written during creation without a demonstrated delivery receipt.
findings.decision: Retain hash/expiry/consumption evidence, keep raw token transient, and reconcile legacy invitations before retiring raw-token storage. Consume under one locked/conditional transaction. Link notification/delivery evidence rather than treating row creation as successful delivery.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass

findings.title: Claims DB, Kysely types and output schema disagree about states
findings.problem: DB allows nine claim states; the authoritative Database ClaimStatus allows only pending/verified/approved/rejected/paid. It cannot represent draft/submitted/sent_back/settled. The output zod enum is also five-state. A separate exported PayClaimsTable has the opposite narrower travel vocabulary and declares budget/reference non-null, while DB permits NULL. These are conflicting contracts, not extra DB columns.
findings.decision: Define one canonical DB row type and explicit supported workflow transitions; align input/output contracts with the intended flow. Filter/route distinct funding flows explicitly; broadening an enum alone does not make the claims API work.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass

findings.title: Financial facts still permit competing or mutable truth
findings.problem: loan_postings has no UPDATE/DELETE rejecting trigger and no unique loan/run key. Claims settlement directly changes loans.outstanding without a posting. payroll_item_lines lacks a closed-run immutability trigger; the header/item guard covers only UPDATE/DELETE. paid_in_run_id and paid_in_batch_id lack the documented payout exclusivity CHECK; a linked obligation is currently labelled paid before actual payment evidence.
findings.decision: The principal, ledger and payout references are legitimate fields. Make immutable postings/payment events authoritative, retain a cache only if explicitly derived and reconcilable, enforce once-only source consumption and closed-result inserts/updates/deletes, and distinguish routed/approved/paid states.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass

findings.title: Known relational/date/money invariants are missing
findings.problem: Several known same-database relations are only BIGINT fields without FK enforcement, including settlement-to-separation and the indicated workflow references. salary_holds has no date-order CHECK. claim_entitlements has neither a nonnegative amount CHECK nor an effective bucket uniqueness/overlap invariant. These omissions leave legitimate fields weakly connected.
findings.decision: Reconcile invalid existing references first, then introduce safe forward constraints and semantic same-owner checks. Choose approved effective-entitlement interval semantics. Polymorphic reference_id/entity_id, external ATS IDs and textual mobile device IDs are not automatically missing-FK defects.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass

findings.title: Claim funding and component ownership remain incomplete
findings.problem: General claim submission omits funding_kind, so the local budget default conflicts with the required budget_id check when no budget is supplied. payout_component_code defaults to REIMB with no FK on that taxonomy field; no REIMB seed exists in the checked payroll code. claim_lines and claim_bills represent travel line items and general bill verification differently; their ownership/payout linkage is not unified.
findings.decision: Preserve both documented funding modes and define required keys per mode. Configure and FK the actual payout component; do not invent a fallback component. Preserve multi-line/multi-currency receipt facts and document ownership, then prove each mode through approval, settlement and one real payout.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass

findings.title: The remaining schema plan has not been implemented or proven as an equivalent contract

findings.title: Future test partitions explain physical growth, not new business fields
findings.problem: Compared with the 13 Oct catalog, 12 new swipe partitions exist, including dates in 2032–2081. Business column definitions are unchanged. Tests use random future dates and the ingestion service creates month partitions; exact causation for each new partition was not traced. This is local test schema growth, not 12 new business models.
findings.decision: Keep test-only provenance clear and bound fixtures/isolate destructive test setup. No production concern is inferred from this user-authorized local test DB. Do not remove append-only evidence or partitions without a reviewed retention/fixture cleanup procedure.
findings.status: Open; audit only, no source/schema repair in this pass
